**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve all event moments in the legacy response**

After interaction activation, an event with more than 50 moments silently loses every older moment from `GET /events/:eventId/moments`. The API still returns a plain array with no cursor or page parameter, and the pre-activation branch below still returns every row, so clients have no way to retrieve the omitted moments; bound each moment's comments/reactions without truncating the event's moment list, or add real pagination.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove legacy follow edges when blocking accounts**

When two accounts already have a `fan_follow` or `party_follow` row, blocking and later unblocking them restores the old relationship automatically: this update clears only `social_v2_pair.follow_a/follow_b`, while `interaction_follows` and `interaction_club_access` continue treating the untouched legacy rows as follower access. That contradicts the account-control promise that unblocking does not restore previous connections and can immediately re-enable follower-only commenting and fan-club writes without a new follow action.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-notify recipients when an edit adds a mention**

When an edited comment newly mentions someone who already received a comment/reply notification for that comment—for example, the publication owner—the cross-kind lookup reuses the existing notification. If that notification was already read, this path neither marks it unread nor updates its type or timestamp, so the newly added mention is silently missed even though edit events explicitly include current mention recipients. Create or refresh an unread mention notification for this case instead of only attaching the actor to the old row.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expose report reasons to moderators**

For reported comments, this inbox returns only the comment body and the number of open reports; the stored `interaction_report.reason` values are never included here or in `interaction_moderation_page`, and the web moderation UI has no other endpoint from which to retrieve them. Moderators therefore must dismiss or remove reports without knowing what users reported, so include the open report reasons in the protected moderation response.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve legacy comments with no author party**

When activation encounters an `event_moment_comment` whose nullable `author_party_id` is `NULL`, this inserts it with `interaction_comment.author_id = NULL`, but canonical readers only return visible comments whose author passes `interaction_actor_live`/`interaction_author_batch`. The legacy endpoint previously returned these rows using `author_name`, so such comments silently disappear after cutover even though the migration counts them as successfully migrated; either retain a readable legacy-author representation or fail activation until these rows are reconciled.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor reply preferences when the reply also mentions its recipient**

When a reply mentions its parent author, that recipient appears with both reply priority 2 and mention priority 3, and `max(priority)` collapses the reasons to `mention`. `interaction_notification_allowed` then checks only the mention preference, so a user with replies enabled but mentions disabled receives no notification for the reply they explicitly opted into. Preserve all applicable reasons or allow delivery when any enabled notification category matches.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow authors to edit after commenting is disabled**

When an owner changes a target to `off`, removes a user from `mentioned`, or the user stops qualifying as a follower, this shared check rejects `comment.edit` even for the existing comment's author. Readers still return `canEdit: true`, so the UI offers editing but every save fails with `comments_not_allowed`; apply `interaction_can_comment` only to creation/replies while retaining the edit-specific author/state checks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enqueue reaction events only when state changes**

When `reaction.set` repeats the actor's current non-null reaction, the preceding `ON CONFLICT ... WHERE` updates no row, but this unconditional result metadata still assigns `eventKind: reaction`; inserting the request then enqueues a notification event. This is particularly reachable through the legacy `active: true` adapter, which creates a fresh request UUID for every call, so a retry can notify the publication owner even though no reaction changed. Only attach the event kind when the insert/update actually affected a row.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh aggregated reaction notifications on new activity**

When a recipient reads the aggregated reaction notification and another actor reacts to the same target within the ten-minute dedupe bucket, this lookup reuses the existing row, but the found branch never marks the underlying `notification` unread or refreshes its timestamp. The new actor is merely attached later, so the unread count remains zero and the owner receives no visible indication of the new reaction; refresh the aggregate when adding new activity.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Surface directory blocks in account controls**

When an existing directory workflow has created a `directory_profile_block` between these parties, `interaction_blocked` denies their interactions, but this list scans only `social_v2_pair`. The account controls therefore show no blocked account—and the block-state/unblock path also operates only on the pair—so the user cannot discover or remove the block that is still preventing interaction. Include actor-owned directory blocks in the projection and define matching unblock behavior, or avoid treating them as account-level interaction blocks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject reaction types outside the selectable set**

An authenticated caller can submit any active published `content_reaction_type`, even if it has no row in `interaction_reaction_choice` and is returned to clients as `selectable: false`. As soon as another catalog option is published, a crafted request can create new reactions that the UI deliberately does not offer; they then appear as historical-looking, nonselectable counts. Validate new reaction values against `interaction_reaction_choice` while continuing to preserve already-migrated historical types.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in forward migration 2026-09-29_interaction_review_repairs (5eb0ac922). Blocking removes both directions from fan_follow and party_follow and clears canonical follow/consent state under account locks. Unblock never recreates these edges. PostgreSQL 16/17 properties cover both stores, unblock, and denied club discussion writes afterward.

Delivery upgrades the existing recipient/comment notification to mention, refreshes timestamp and unread state once per event, and leaves unchanged mentions quiet. PostgreSQL 16/17 tests cover already-read owner notifications, retained notification identity and a second edit with the same mention.

Fixed in 5eb0ac922 / 3ecbf3a12 and native PR120. Both moderator queues return up to the latest 20 open report reasons (total shown), without reporter identities; non-moderator owners receive none. Web and native show the reasons before decisions. SQL permission tests pass on PostgreSQL 16/17; rendered moderator-decision flows pass on both clients (native full suite: 532 tests).

Fixed with the fail-safe option in 5eb0ac922. First activation now rejects NULL or unresolved legacy author identities before any canonical conversion. A regression inserts an anonymous historical comment, proves the whole activation rolls back with source/mapping/activation state preserved, then runs the nonempty valid migration. The runbook requires trusted identity reconciliation, never invented attribution. Both PG16 and restored-production PG17 checks pass; the restored live source has no such comments.

Fixed in 5eb0ac922: candidate reasons are retained per recipient and delivery picks the strongest enabled applicable reason after current privacy/visibility checks. A generated eight-combination preference truth table proves disabled mentions retain enabled reply/comment delivery and all-disabled sends nothing. PG16 and restored-production PG17 pass.

Fixed in 5eb0ac922. The creation policy applies only to comment.create; edits still require the live author, accessible target, visible comment, no block and expected version. SQL regressions cover edit after off and mentioned-policy changes while rejecting new comments. Both PG16/17 pass.

Fixed in 5eb0ac922: capture FOUND immediately after the reaction upsert and enqueue reaction activity only on a real state change. The legacy engagement projection uses the same flag. A fresh-request-key desired-state retry is tested to produce no event, no unread refresh and unchanged counters; concurrent reaction properties remain green on the canonical command.

Fixed in 5eb0ac922: an event watermark on the aggregate refreshes unread state and timestamp for genuinely new activity, while replayed/older events cannot resurrect read state. Tests mark the aggregate read, add a second actor in the bucket, require unread+new timestamp, then mark read and replay dispatch without changes. PG16/17 pass.

Fixed in 5eb0ac922. Account list/state include actor-owned directory blocks. Unblock removes only that actor subject-profile direction and retains peer-owned blocks. After activation, directory writes share party locks, advance the canonical revision and sever legacy/canonical follows. PG16/17 regressions cover list privacy, stale revisions, both blocking directions, effective unblock and no restored follow.

Fixed in 5eb0ac922: new reaction choices require interaction_reaction_choice in addition to active/published catalog state. Migration and readers continue preserving historical nonselectable types, and removal remains available. SQL tests reject an active catalog type absent from selectable choices; nonempty historical migration tests still pass on PG16/17.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require publication authority for artist updates**

For any `social_sync_post` associated with an artist profile, this branch unconditionally marks the target public, so an anonymous caller can enumerate `/public/interactions/targets/artist_update/<id>` and retrieve the stored caption preview, artist association, and route. The existing post-list endpoint is protected by `ensureSocialSyncAccess` in `TDF.Server.SocialSync`, and there is no public renderer or publication state for these rows, so ingestion alone should not grant public visibility or allow interaction threads; require an explicit public/reviewed authority or keep this target kind unavailable.

body: Fixed in 3ecbf3a12: preserve every accessible legacy moment and batch previews into one database query, bounding per-moment comments/reactions. The real HTTP regression seeds 60 moments and requires all 60 distinct IDs. Hosted backend job 109187113814 passed the full build and HTTP suite with this regression.

Fixed in d6c52fad1 / 472dfa670 (published in current head090b5a132). Forward migration139 disables artist_update and its resolver always returns unavailable, even if the capability flag is re-enabled. Ingestion is never publication authority. SQL tests cover anonymous and owner denial, capability-toggle resistance and preserved imported caption; PostgreSQL16 and restored-production PostgreSQL17.8 pass, including repeat migration. Anonymous/authenticated HTTP denial checks are included in current hosted qualification. Existing published artist-release and club-post paths are unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow users to withdraw reactions after losing write access**

When an actor already has a reaction and later loses club follow/officer eligibility, `interaction_domain_write(target,actor)` becomes false, so this condition rejects even `reaction.set` with `reactionTypeId: null`. The summary also exposes `canReact: false`, disabling the selected reaction button, leaving the reaction counted and causing it to reappear if access is restored. Apply the domain-write/selectability requirement only when setting a non-null reaction, while allowing the current actor to delete their existing reaction from an otherwise accessible target.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 7d8de4c5d and registered by c2fe7babf. The forward migration applies domain-write/selectability requirements only to non-null selection; withdrawal retains current visibility, blocking, live-account/session and actor-slot guards. Summary canReact permits an existing slot while every new choice becomes nonselectable after eligibility loss, so both current clients expose only removal. SQL properties and real HTTP verify revocation, own-slot isolation, rejected selection, idempotent withdrawal, counters and no resurrection after following again; the rendered web regression verifies selected removal and disabled alternatives. All seven local database suites/concurrency, the PostgreSQL17 production-restore rehearsal, eight rendered tests and82 release tests pass. Hosted final CI is running.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep blocked authors within moderation reach**

When a comment author blocks the publication owner or a platform moderator after posting, this shared guard rejects `comment.hide`, `comment.remove`, `comment.restore`, and `comment.report.resolve`. The same blocked-author predicate in `interaction_moderation_page` and `interaction_report_inbox` also removes the comment from their queues, while other users can still see it. An abusive commenter can therefore evade moderation by blocking the people responsible for moderation; privileged moderation operations and queues should not be suppressed by the moderator's bilateral block state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in e2dc17a51 and registered by 0f99959fa. Scoped owner hide/restore and moderator removal/report resolution no longer fail due to an author block; current target access, live account/session, role, expected version and audit requirements remain. Authorized queues retain evidence and actual moderation state, while ordinary lists still filter blocks. Exact report links resolve to redacted context so the authorized queue remains reachable. Owners gain no administrator powers. Web and native queues now expose owner hide for blocked visible comments (mobile PR121). Actual SQL properties and real local HTTP exercise blocking both owner/moderator, normal-read privacy, queue evidence, redacted links, owner hide/restore, moderator resolution/removal, denied owner admin removal and erasure/audit. Nine rendered flows per client, local database/concurrency, release checks and PostgreSQL17 restored-production moderation properties pass; final hosted/artifact qualification is running.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve moderator access when the publication owner blocks them**

If a publication owner blocks a platform moderator, `interaction_target_context` returns NULL because the resolver applies the owner's bilateral block, so this early return prevents `comment.remove` and `comment.report.resolve`; the same context requirement also removes every comment on that target from the global report inbox and moderation page. + WHEN 'event' THEN
+   SELECT CASE WHEN e.organizer_party_id ~ '^[1-9][0-9]{0,17}$' THEN e.organizer_party_id::bigint END,
+     e.title,'/eventos/'||e.id,coalesce(v.public_share_eligible,false)
+   INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value,public_value FROM social_event e
+   LEFT JOIN directory_public_rsvp_event v ON v.id=e.id WHERE e.id=entity::bigint;
+   visible:=FOUND AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM social_event e WHERE e.id=entity::bigint AND interaction_event_access(e.id,actor));
+ WHEN 'event_moment' THEN
+   SELECT CASE WHEN m.author_party_id ~ '^[1-9][0-9]{0,17}$' THEN m.author_party_id::bigint END,
+     coalesce(m.caption,'Momento'),'/eventos/'||e.id||'?moment='||m.id,
+     coalesce(v.public_share_eligible,false)
+   INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value,public_value FROM event_moment m
+   JOIN social_event e ON e.id=m.event_id LEFT JOIN directory_public_rsvp_event v ON v.id=e.id
+   WHERE m.id=entity::bigint;
+   -- A moment's author does not gain access to its private parent event.
+   visible:=FOUND AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM event_moment m WHERE m.id=entity::bigint AND interaction_event_access(m.event_id,actor));
+ WHEN 'recording' THEN
+   SELECT r.created_by,r.title_es,'/records?recording='||r.id INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value
+   FROM recording r JOIN workflow_state s ON s.id=r.workflow_state_id
+   WHERE r.id=entity::uuid AND r.active AND s.active AND s.code='published';
+   public_value:=FOUND; visible:=public_value;
+ WHEN 'recording_session' THEN
+   SELECT r.created_by,r.title_es,'/records?session='||r.id INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value
+   FROM recording_session r JOIN workflow_state s ON s.id=r.workflow_state_id
+   WHERE r.id=entity::uuid AND r.active AND s.active AND s.code='published';
+   public_value:=FOUND; visible:=public_value;
+ WHEN 'record_release' THEN
+   SELECT r.created_by,r.title_es,'/records?release='||r.id INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value
+   FROM record_release r JOIN workflow_state s ON s.id=r.workflow_state_id
+   WHERE r.id=entity::uuid AND r.active AND s.active AND s.code='published';
+   public_value:=FOUND; visible:=public_value;
+ WHEN 'artist_release' THEN
+   SELECT r.artist_party_id,r.title,'/artista/'||r.artist_party_id||'?release='||r.id
+   INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value FROM artist_release r
+   JOIN artist_profile a ON a.artist_party_id=r.artist_party_id WHERE r.id=entity::bigint;
+   public_value:=FOUND; visible:=public_value;
+ WHEN 'artist_update' THEN
+   SELECT p.artist_party_id,left(coalesce(p.caption,'Actualización'),160),
+     '/artista/'||p.artist_party_id||'?update='||p.id
+   INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value FROM social_sync_post p
+   JOIN artist_profile a ON a.artist_party_id=p.artist_party_id WHERE p.id=entity::bigint;
+   public_value:=FOUND; visible:=public_value;
+ WHEN 'directory_profile' THEN
+   SELECT p.subject_party_id,p.public_name,'/directorio/'||p.slug,p.id,
+     EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM directory_public_profile v WHERE v.id=p.id)
+   INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value,profile,public_value
+   FROM directory_profile p WHERE p.id=entity::uuid AND p.canonical_profile_id IS NULL
+     AND p.archived_at IS NULL AND p.suspended_at IS NULL AND p.moderation_status='allowed';
+   visible:=FOUND AND public_value;
+ WHEN 'classified' THEN
+   SELECT p.subject_party_id,c.title,'/clasificados/'||c.slug,p.id,
+     c.status='published' AND c.moderation_status='allowed'
+       AND (c.expires_at IS NULL OR c.expires_at>now())
+       AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM directory_public_profile v WHERE v.id=p.id)
+   INTO owner_id,title_value,route_value,profile,public_value
+   FROM classified c JOIN directory_profile p ON p.id=c.author_profile_id WHERE c.id=entity::uuid;
+   visible:=FOUND AND public_value;
+ ELSE RETURN NULL;
+ END CASE;
+ IF club IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM fan_club c WHERE c.id=club
+   AND (interaction_blocked(actor,c.artist_party_id) OR NOT interaction_owner_live(c.artist_party_id))) THEN RETURN NULL; END IF;
+ IF visible IS DISTINCT FROM true OR NOT interaction_owner_live(owner_id)
+   OR interaction_blocked(actor,owner_id) THEN RETURN NULL; END IF;
+ IF actor IS NOT NULL AND NOT interaction_actor_live(actor) THEN RETURN NULL; END IF;
+ manage:=actor IS NOT NULL AND (actor=owner_id OR (club IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM fan_club c WHERE c.id=club AND (c.artist_party_id=actor OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM fan_club_officer o WHERE o.club_id=club AND o.fan_party_id=actor AND (o.term_ends_at IS NULL OR o.term_ends_at>now()))))) OR (profile IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS(
+   SELECT 1 FROM directory_profile_manager m WHERE m.profile_id=profile
+     AND m.account_party_id=actor AND m.active AND m.can_manage)));
+ RETURN jsonb_build_object('kind',kind,'key',entity,'ownerId',owner_id,
+   'title',title_value,'route',route_value,'public',public_value,'canManage',coalesce(manage,false),
+   'reactable',k.reactable,'commentable',k.commentable,'shareable',k.shareable);
+END $$;
+
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION interaction_target_context(target uuid,actor bigint)
+RETURNS jsonb LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
+ SELECT interaction_resolve(t.entity_kind,t.entity_key,actor)
+ FROM interaction_target t WHERE t.id=target AND t.retired_at IS NULL
+$$;
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION interaction_follows(actor bigint,owner_id bigint) RETURNS boolean
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
+ SELECT actor=owner_id OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM social_v2_pair p
+   WHERE p.party_a=least(actor,owner_id) AND p.party_b=greatest(actor,owner_id)
+     AND CASE WHEN actor=p.party_a THEN p.follow_a ELSE p.follow_b END
+     AND NOT (p.block_a OR p.block_b))
+   OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM fan_follow WHERE fan_party_id=actor AND artist_party_id=owner_id)
+   OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM party_follow WHERE follower_party_id=actor AND following_party_id=owner_id)
+$$;
+-- Club reading is available to authenticated users in the existing API. Its
+-- posting/reaction boundary requires following the artist (or artist/officer).
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION interaction_domain_write(target uuid,actor bigint) RETURNS boolean
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
+ SELECT CASE t.entity_kind
+ WHEN 'club_post' THEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM fan_club_post p WHERE p.id=t.entity_key::bigint AND interaction_club_access(actor,p.club_id))
+ WHEN 'club_memory' THEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM fan_club_memory m JOIN fan_club_member_profile p ON p.id=m.member_profile_id
+   WHERE m.id=t.entity_key::bigint AND interaction_club_access(actor,p.club_id))
+ ELSE true END FROM interaction_target t WHERE t.id=target
+$$;
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION interaction_can_comment(target uuid,actor bigint) RETURNS boolean
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
+ WITH context AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT interaction_target_context(target,actor) AS value)
+ SELECT coalesce(interaction_actor_live(actor) AND c.value IS NOT NULL
+   AND interaction_domain_write(target,actor) AND (c.value->>'commentable')::boolean AND CASE t.comment_policy
+     WHEN 'off' THEN false
+     WHEN 'everyone' THEN true
+     WHEN 'followers' THEN interaction_follows(actor,(c.value->>'ownerId')::bigint)
+     WHEN 'mentioned' THEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM interaction_target_mention m
+       WHERE m.target_id=t.id AND m.party_id=actor)
+     ELSE false END,false)
+ FROM interaction_target t CROSS JOIN context c WHERE t.id=target
+$$;
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION interaction_register(kind text,entity text,actor bigint)
+RETURNS uuid LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
+DECLARE target uuid; context jsonb;
+BEGIN
+ context:=interaction_resolve(kind,entity,actor);
+ IF context IS NULL THEN RETURN NULL; END IF;
+ entity:=context->>'key';
+ INSERT INTO interaction_target(entity_kind,entity_key) VALUES(kind,entity)
+   ON CONFLICT(entity_kind,entity_key) DO NOTHING;
